title: UNEP records eight methane mitigations in Turkmenistan after MARS notifications
summary: UNEP lists eight mitigation cases, with site identifiers and dates from November 2024 to March 2026. The contribution of AI is described at system level, rather than isolated for each repair.
account: UNEP’s MARS mitigation index lists eight Turkmenistan cases: two in Yelguyi in November 2024, Babarap in June 2025, Gugurtli field in July 2025, Balguyy in August 2025, two in Dauletabad in February 2026, and Lebap Province in March 2026. Each entry has a source identifier and a link to an individual case document. UNEP describes these as mitigations that its notification and monitoring system helped prompt and verify. UNEP states that MARS combines satellite observations, scientific review, and AI to identify emissions for government and company action. The available aggregate evidence does not isolate AI’s contribution from analysts, notifications, and physical repairs or quantify their combined benefit.
purpose: Satellite-based detection and notification of large methane plumes so that governments and operators mitigate them. The reported repairs are that purpose.
system: UNEP IMEO Methane Alert and Response System (MARS): satellite plume detection and analysis with AI models, notification and satellite confirmation
deployer: UNEP International Methane Emissions Observatory (notification); Government of Turkmenistan and its oil and gas operators (repairs; entities not named in cited sources)
location: Turkmenistan: Yelguyi, Babarap, Gugurtli field, Balguyy, Dauletabad, and Lebap Province
domain: Climate change mitigation / methane emissions monitoring
segment: Oil and gas sector; intergovernmental observatory
